commitResults.messageBody:
Add task serialization and a storage utility that rewrites the data file
after tasks are added, marked, unmarked, or deleted. Update the UI test plan to verify persistence does not alter console output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement loading saved tasks when the application starts
commitResults.messageBody: Read tasks from the data file and reconstruct their types and completion statuses at startup. Isolate UI test data and add coverage for loading saved todos, deadlines, and events.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle storage errors and edge cases
commitResults.messageBody:
Validate saved task records and report malformed or inaccessible data
with helpful messages. Save through a temporary file, roll back
in-memory changes when persistence fails, and expand UI tests for
storage edge cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-7'
commitResults.messageBody:
Save and load tasks from disk, validate stored records, handle storage
failures safely, and add UI tests for persistence and error cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement LocalDate support for tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Parse ISO-formatted dates, display them in a user-friendly format, validate invalid dates, and update storage loading and UI tests accordingly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add time support for scheduled tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Store deadline and event schedules as LocalDateTime, accept both ISO dates and d/M/yyyy HHmm input, preserve compatibility with existing saved dates, and update UI tests for timed schedules.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to find scheduled tasks by date
commitResults.messageBody: Implement the on command to list deadlines and events occurring on a specified date, including multi-day event ranges, while preserving original task numbers and handling invalid or unmatched dates.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-8'
commitResults.messageBody:
Store deadline and event schedules as LocalDateTime, support date-only
and timed input formats, display schedules clearly, preserve
compatibility with existing saved dates, and add an on command to find
scheduled tasks occurring on a specific date.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract console lifecycle into Ui
commitResults.messageBody:
Move greeting, command input, separators, error display, and farewell
behavior out of Peter so the main class can focus on application flow.
Preserve the existing console output and command-loop behavior while
establishing a dedicated UI boundary for future refactoring.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make Storage an application dependency
commitResults.messageBody:
Give Storage an explicit data-file path and convert load and save
operations from static methods to instance behavior. Let Peter own its
Storage, Ui, and loaded tasks through a constructor, separating persistence
configuration from application flow while preserving existing behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
Move command recognition, task creation, date parsing, field validation,
and task-number validation out of Peter and into a dedicated Parser class.
Simplify Peter to dispatch parsed commands and execute their operations
while preserving all existing console behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task collection into TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
Peter holds a raw ArrayList<Task> and calls it directly for
every list operation.

The collection has no owner, so list concerns are tangled into
command dispatch.

Move it into TaskList, exposing only size, get, add,
add-at-index, delete, and setDone; delegate from Peter.

Keep the interface narrow so TaskList stays sole owner;
asList() gives Storage a read-only view.

All 17 UI test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move task output into Ui
commitResults.messageBody:
Peter prints task confirmations, listings, and date queries with
System.out.println.

Presentation logic sits in the coordinator while Ui already owns
console output, so display code cannot change independently and
no single class controls the console.

Add showTaskList, showAddedTask, showRemovedTask,
showTaskStatusChange, and showTasksOnDate to Ui, and call them
from Peter.

Give Ui a private formatTask helper. The type/status/description
/schedule form was repeated at four call sites; centralising it
leaves one place to change how a task reads.

System.out now appears only in Ui. All 17 UI test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract commands into Command classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Peter dispatches on the command word in a seven-case switch and
holds a private helper for each modifying command.

Adding a command means editing the switch, adding a helper, and
touching the parser, so command behaviour is spread across three
places and Peter grows with every feature.

Add an abstract Command with execute(TaskList, Ui, Storage) and
isExit(), plus AddCommand, DeleteCommand, MarkCommand,
ListCommand, FindOnDateCommand, and ExitCommand. Return one from
Parser.parse and have run() execute whatever it gets.

Put the save-then-undo shape in Command.saveOrRollback so each
subclass supplies only the rollback that reverses its own change,
rather than repeating the try/catch three times.

Mark and delete keep the raw command text and resolve the task
number during execute, because the "no tasks" and range checks
need a task count the parser does not have. run() also keeps a
hasNextCommand guard so piped input ending without bye does not
throw. All 17 UI test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-MoreOOP'
Move all classes into the peter package
commitResults.messageBody:
All 19 classes sit in the default package at the source root, mixed
with stale .class files.

The default package gives them no namespace and no structure to grow
into as classes are added.

Move every class into a peter package under src/main/java, add the
package declaration to each file, remove the stale build output, and
ignore *.class repository-wide.

Keep one flat package so this stays a pure move: same-package classes
still see each other, so no imports or access modifiers change.

Update the build and run commands in test/ui-test-plan.md, since the
entry point is now peter.Peter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split the peter package into task, command, ui, and storage
commitResults.messageBody:
All 19 classes sit in one flat peter package.

A flat package gives no grouping, so related classes are hard to
find and the growing set of command classes is not separated from
the task model.

Split the classes into peter.task, peter.command, peter.ui, and
peter.storage, and add the imports each package now needs.

Keep Parser and PeterException in the root package: the commands
call back into Parser at execute time, so a peter.parser package
would depend on peter.command and be depended on by it.

No member needed widening, since everything used across the new
boundaries was already public. Update the test plan's javac line to recurse into the subpackages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Packages'
Merge branch 'add-gradle-support' into branch-A-Gradle
Update build.gradle main class to Peter
Merge branch 'branch-A-Gradle'
Add JUnit tests for ScheduleDateTime
commitResults.messageBody:
ScheduleDateTime parses and formats every schedule value in the
app, yet has no tests. Both parse methods fall back between two
formats, and format() branches on midnight.

These branches fail quietly. A relaxed resolver would shift an
invalid date instead of rejecting it, and a locale slip would
change AM/PM output, with nothing to catch either.

Add ScheduleDateTimeTest covering all four public methods: valid
and rejected inputs, the midnight and noon boundaries, null
handling, and parse/format round trips.

Test this class first because it is pure static functions with no
console, file, or clock dependency, so the cases need no fixtures
or mocks.

All 43 tests pass. No production code changes, so the UI test plan
is unaffected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for parser, storage, and task classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Parser and Storage hold the most
branching in the app, and the task classes define the save format
and date matching.

A wrong error message, an off-by-one date boundary, or a drifting
save format breaks the app quietly, with nothing to catch it.

Add tests for Parser, Storage, TaskList, Todo, Deadline, and
Event: command routing, argument errors, corrupt save files, date
ranges, and save/load round trips.

Target the highest-value half of the methods and skip Ui, whose
console output the UI test plan already covers. Point the storage
tests at @TempDir so they never touch real data.

197 tests pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enhance code logic that rejects backwards events and fix error message typo
commitResults.messageBody:
Parser accepts an event whose end precedes its start, and the
storage-delimiter error is missing a space after "Oh dear!".

A backwards event covers no dates, so it never matches 'on': the
task saves but the user can never find it again.

Reject an event whose end falls before its start, and add the
missing space.

Compare with isBefore so a zero-length event stays legal. Guard in
the parser only, since every saved event passes through it and
storage cannot receive a backwards one.

Update the affected unit tests and the event and delimiter cases in the UI test plan. 200 tests pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-JUnit'
Rename the shadow JAR to peter.jar
Merge branch 'branch-A-Jar'
Add JavaDoc comments across the remaining public methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Six classes carry no member comments at all, and Task documents
only two of its ten non-private members. Its protected fields and the occursOn overrides that decide date matching are undocumented.

A reader cannot tell from the code that description must exclude
the storage delimiter, that Deadline matches only its own date, or
that Event's range is inclusive at both ends.

Document every remaining non-private class, method, field, and
enum constant, favouring the reasons a reader cannot infer over
restating names.

Use {@inheritDoc} on overrides so each parent contract stays in one
place, and record on Event's constructor that it deliberately skips
the date-order check that Parser performs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the current code to comply with java coding standard
Add a coding standard skill and mandate its use
commitResults.messageBody:
Java style rules live only in reviewers' heads, and AGENTS.md asks
for Javadoc without saying which convention governs the rest.

Without a written standard, each change picks its own naming,
import order, and Javadoc wording, and reviews relitigate style.

Capture the se-education.org intermediate Java standard as the
seedu-java-coding-standard skill, and require it in AGENTS.md for
every file under src/main/java and src/test/java.

Store it as a skill rather than inline in AGENTS.md so the full
rules load only when Java is being written, and place it under
.claude/skills so the tooling actually discovers it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a Git convention skill and mandate its use
commitResults.messageBody:
AGENTS.md asks for commit messages with enough rationale but names
no convention, and the Git rules live only in chat history.

Without a written convention, subject mood, length limits, and body
structure are decided afresh each commit and drift apart.

Capture the se-education.org Git convention as the seedu-git-standard
skill, and require it in AGENTS.md for every commit, branch, and tag.

Store it as a skill so the full rules load only when a commit is
being written, mirroring seedu-java-coding-standard.

The guide is silent on tags and pull requests, so the existing
lightweight-tag rule is recorded in the skill as a project addition.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to find tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks can only be listed in full or filtered by date, so a user
with a long list has no way to locate one by what it says.

Recalling a task means scanning the whole list by eye, which gets
worse as the list grows.

Add a find command that lists the tasks whose descriptions contain
a keyword, reporting when nothing matches.

Mirror the existing on command: a predicate on Task, a Ui method
that renders the results, and a read-only Command. Match case
insensitively on any substring, and keep original task numbers so
a match can be marked or deleted straight away.

Add unit tests for keyword matching and find parsing, and a UI test
plan case. 216 tests pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-CodingStandard'
Merge branch 'branch-Level-9'
Merge branch 'branch-A-JavaDoc'
Add Checkstyle to enforce the Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
The build has no automated style checking, so conformance to the
se-education.org intermediate Java coding standard is verified only
by eye.

Manual checking is unreliable and lets violations such as wildcard
imports, missing braces and over-long lines reach the repository
unnoticed.

Apply the Gradle checkstyle plugin with a rule set that encodes the
coding standard, and suppress Javadoc requirements for test classes.

Keep the rules in config/checkstyle so the same configuration is
shared by the Gradle build and any IDE plugin, rather than being
duplicated per developer. Test classes are suppressed because their
purpose is evident from their names and a class header adds noise.

Checkstyle now runs as part of the standard check and build tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix Checkstyle violations in task and test code
commitResults.messageBody:
Task declares hasKeyword twice with identical bodies, and the test
classes wrap assertThrows lambdas before the arrow.

Checkstyle now runs as part of the build, and both patterns fail it,
so the build is red until they are cleaned up. The duplicated method
is also a maintenance hazard: a future edit to one copy would
silently diverge from the other.

Delete the redundant hasKeyword declaration, and move the lambda
arrow onto the line that opens the wrap.

Keep the first declaration with its Javadoc so the documented
behaviour survives unchanged, and follow the standard's rule that a
wrapped line breaks after the operator rather than before it.

The changes are formatting and duplicate removal only; no behaviour
is affected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-CheckStyle'
Duplicate project skills into .agents directory
commitResults.messageBody:
The two mandatory project standards, Java coding and Git, live only
under .claude/skills, so only Claude Code discovers them.

Other agent tools look for skills under .agents/skills, so when the
project is opened with one of them, code and commit messages get
written without the standards in effect.

Add copies of both SKILL.md files under .agents/skills.

Copy rather than symlink: symlinks are not reliably reproduced on
Windows checkouts and Git records them inconsistently across
platforms, so a plain file is the simplest portable option.

The copies are byte-identical to the .claude versions today; both
locations must be updated together whenever a standard changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaFX dependencies to the build
commitResults.messageBody:
The build declares no UI toolkit, so the app can only ever present a
console interface.

Level 10 requires a desktop GUI, which needs JavaFX on the compile and
runtime classpath before any UI code can be written.

Add the JavaFX base, controls, fxml and graphics artifacts, and ignore
the editor's .vscode directory.

Declare all three platform classifiers rather than using the JavaFX
Gradle plugin, so the same build and the same shadowJar work on
Windows, macOS and Linux without per-machine configuration.

No application code changes yet; the text UI still runs unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command responses as strings
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui writes every message directly to System.out, and Command.execute
returns nothing, so a caller has no way to obtain the text of a
response.

A graphical interface must place each response into its own dialog
bubble, which requires the response as a value rather than as a side
effect on the console.

Route Ui output through an injectable stream, and add methods that
return the greeting, the startup loading error, and the result of
one command as strings.

Injecting the stream is the smallest change that serves both callers:
the console keeps its existing Ui, while a caller wanting the text
supplies a buffer instead. Command and its subclasses are untouched.
Errors are returned as text rather than thrown, since a caller
rendering a reply has nowhere to handle an exception.

Console output is unchanged, so the UI test plan still passes and the
text UI remains the easier way to test the core logic. Add unit tests
for the new methods.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a minimal JavaFX window
commitResults.messageBody:
The application has no graphical interface, so the chatbot can only
be used from CLI.

Level 10 requires a desktop app, and proving the window, the FXML and
the chatbot are correctly connected before any styling is added keeps
a wiring mistake easy to isolate.

Add a launcher, an Application subclass, a main window controller and
its FXML, and point the application plugin at the launcher.

The launcher exists only because a main class extending Application
refuses to start when JavaFX is on the classpath rather than the
module path. The chatbot reaches the controller through a setter,
since FXMLLoader creates controllers with a no-arg constructor.

Responses render as plain labels for now. The console entry point is
unchanged, but the UI test plan now compiles with Gradle: a bare
javac cannot resolve the new JavaFX imports, and only the build knows
where those jars live.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show responses as dialog boxes with avatars
commitResults.messageBody:
Responses render as bare labels stacked in a column, so a reply is
not visually distinguishable from the command that produced it.

A chat interface is only readable when each turn is attributed, which
needs a per-turn component carrying a picture alongside wrapped text.

Add a reusable dialog box component with user and chatbot variants,
and the two avatar images it displays.

Use the fx:root pattern so the component is its own root and its own
controller, which is what lets it be created once per message rather
than once by the loader. Named static factories keep the two variants
readable where the transcript is built.

commitResults.messageTitle: Greet on startup and exit on the bye command
commitResults.messageBody:
The window opens empty and stays open after bye, which prints a
farewell that leads nowhere. A data file that fails to load is not
reported at all.

A chatbot that says goodbye without closing is confusing, and after a
failed load the window would accept commands against an empty list
and overwrite the saved file on the first change.

Show the greeting when the window opens, report a loading failure and
refuse further commands, and close the window shortly after bye.

Delay the exit with a timer rather than a sleep, which would freeze
the window instead of showing the farewell. Disabling the controls
after a loading failure mirrors the console, which reports the error
and stops rather than continuing with unknown tasks.

The bye command is kept rather than removed, so closing the app by
typing a command stays consistent with its CLI-style UX.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add manual GUI checklist to UI test plan
Merge branch 'branch-Level-10'
Use var-args where callers know their arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList needs a separate no-arg constructor, Ui prints multi-line
messages as runs of separate statements, and Parser builds a String
array literal only to loop over it once.

Each of these is a fixed argument list written out at the call site,
so the surrounding ceremony adds nothing a reader needs.

Take var-args in a single TaskList constructor, in a new Ui method
for printing several lines, and in the Parser helper that matches a
command word.

Keep the TaskList overload taking a List, since storage loads a
number of tasks it cannot know until run time, which is what a
collection parameter is for. Leave bye and list on their own exact
match so a trailing argument stays unrecognised.

Behaviour is unchanged: gradlew check passes and all 18 console
cases in the UI test plan produce identical output.
